title: The Blending Ratio Is Not Where the Performance Is: Diagnosing Prototype Blending for Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.23634v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Many few-shot adaptation methods for vision-language models classify with a convex combination of the zero-shot text prototype and the mean of the K labelled image features, with a single blending ratio routinely tuned on held-out labels, often on the test set itself. We ask what the family's own bias-variance justification invites: what is the right ratio, can it be estimated without validation data, and is finding it where the performance is? First, the ratio minimising prototype mean-squared error has a closed form whose support-set plug-in is exactly a positive-part James-Stein coefficient shrinking towards the text prototype. Across 4,800 cells (ten datasets, five backbones including SigLIP, five shot counts, five seeds, four prompt tiers) this theoretically optimal ratio is a reliable estimate of the wrong quantity: on the 950 primary-tier cells where it is defined it trails a test-set-oracle ratio by 8.5 points. translated_title: 混合比例并非性能关键：诊断视觉-语言模型少样本适应中的原型混合
translated_abstract: 许多视觉-语言模型的少样本适应方法使用零样本文本原型与K个带标签图像特征均值的凸组合进行分类，其中单个混合比例通常根据保留标签（常常在测试集本身）进行调优。我们探究该系列方法自身偏差-方差论证所引出的问题：正确的比例是什么？能否在没有验证数据的情况下估计？找到这个比例是否就是性能所在？首先，使原型均方误差最小的比例具有闭式解，其支持集代入恰好是向文本原型收缩的正部分James-Stein系数。在4,800个单元（十个数据集、五个骨干网络包括SigLIP、五种样本数量、五个随机种子、四种提示层级）中，这一理论最优比例是对错误量的可靠估计：在950个主要层级单元中，它比测试集最优比例落后8.5个百分点。它接近饱和。
tldr: 该论文发现原型混合比例的理论最优估计并非性能关键，测试集调优比例仍显著更优，质疑了少样本适应中依赖混合比例的常见做法。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that the theoretically optimal prototype blending ratio is not where performance lies, as test-set-tuned ratios still significantly outperform it, questioning the common reliance on blending ratios in few-shot adaptation.
